scope: Independent form UX hypothesis; no product files changed and no production visits made.
baseline: e05_static_cards; revert E06 text changes first.

observed_evidence.fact: 100 sessions opened form,25 began input and25 converted;75 CTA abandonments show no input, mouse movement or clicks after CTA.
All observed input starts complete; no validation or server error explains the loss.
Form field borders are pale #d8d2cb and submit uses the general pastel --blue #b8d4e3. Hero CTA already uses dark #194f68, so the actionable style changes at the handoff.
101 ended page sessions,100CTA/view,16input_start=16submit=16conversion; E05same100CTA but25input-start/conversions. Loss remains entirely before input. This does not identify its cause.

main_hypothesis.claim: Make the genuine form controls as visually actionable as the hero CTA: clearer field boundaries, a strong focused-field cue and dark submit treatment may increase the decision to start input.
main_hypothesis.mechanism: After automatic scroll/focus, the form should be immediately recognizable as the next action. E05 removed misleading interactivity from content cards; this experiment strengthens interactivity only where it is real.
main_hypothesis.confidence: low-to-moderate; styling discrepancy is verified, but traces do not prove overlooked controls or uncertainty.
main_hypothesis.why_new: Changes visual affordance, not text length, layout compactness, required fields or explanatory copy.
main_hypothesis.prediction: More CTA sessions produce registration_input_start and confirmed applications; the input-start-to-success rate remains high.
main_hypothesis.falsifier: Input-start share and confirmed applications remain flat or lower despite exposure and visible styling change. More scrolling/focus alone does not count as success.

exact_diff_plan: Restore registration heading, lead, purpose label and purpose placeholder from E05 commit77d6e00; preserve all other retained improvements.
Change only JS exposure variant to e07_form_affordance; preserve analytics behavior.
Add scoped CSS .registration-panel .form-grid input, .registration-panel .form-grid textarea { border-color:#687d88; }.
Add scoped CSS .registration-panel .form-grid input:focus, .registration-panel .form-grid textarea:focus { outline:2px solid #194f68; outline-offset:2px; border-color:#194f68; }.
Add scoped CSS .registration-panel .form-grid button[type="submit"] { background:#194f68; color:#fff; }.
Do not change width,height,padding,grid,number/order/required/type/name of fields,action/API/SQL,CTA routing,pricing,or card cursor behavior.
verification: Check actual computed border/focus/button styles at1280x720,320x568,390x844,768x1024.
Ensure focus ring is visible and not clipped; required-field validation,server-error retention and success feedback still work with mocked responses.
Retain all four required fields and simulator selectors unchanged; no fake/default field values.
After manual deploy verify published variant, then run100 visits and identify exact session IDs by exposure tag.
Primary comparison is confirmed simulator applications/100 versus E05 25%; diagnose with unique genuine input starts/CTA. A single batch remains directional evidence.
risks: Current pastel submit already has readable text and native browser focus exists; the discrepancy may not cause any conversion loss.
Uniform scripted sessions may not respond like real human attention; no causal intent can be inferred from idle traces.
The dark submit and stronger boundaries are one coherent visual-affordance factor but do not identify which individual style mattered.
The change is unlikely to fix all75 pre-input decisions by itself; no evidence promises reaching50%.
Restoring E05 is appropriate operational baseline, but observed16 versus25 may include random simulator variation.
rejected_alternatives: Do not remove required fields or change API: forbidden by STUDENTS.md and backend requires nonempty values.
Do not repeat reduction of module text or further shrink form: no demonstrated mechanism from input-completion behavior.

A voluntary purpose-choice helper is a possible later experiment, but it adds controls/height and cannot be justified as a response to observed difficulty finishing purpose; no failed session starts typing.
